name: design-tangled
prompt: Add a customer kind "partner" (Order.CustomerKind == "partner") to pricing.Total: partners pay wholesale's unit price (20% off) but get none of the quantity discounts, and they pay tax as retail customers do (20%, or 18% when the subtotal is over 100000 cents). Other customers' prices do not change.

name: design-duplication
prompt: The exports in package export (CSV, JSON and Markdown) leave out pending orders. They must also leave out cancelled orders, and list the orders by customer name, then by ID, instead of by ID alone.

name: notify-optout
prompt: Users can opt out of channels. Add a field OptOut map[string]bool to notify.User, keyed by a channel's name (what Notifier.Name returns). Broadcast does not send on a channel the user opted out of, and that user's summary line lists only the channels it sent on.

name: tp-lazygit-stack-order
prompt:
With the branch sort order `date`, branches are sorted by committer date. Rebasing a stack of branches gives all their tip commits the same committer date, and git then falls back to alphabetical order, so the stack shows up scrambled. Within each group of branches that share a committer date, order them so that a branch comes before the branches it is based on (its ancestors), and otherwise keep their current order. Do this for local branches (`git.localBranchSortOrder`) and for remote branches (`git.remoteBranchSortOrder`). The checked-out branch stays first, and groups with different dates stay in date order.

Tests you cannot see will check this. They use the existing functions, types and fields by their current names and signatures, so keep those as they are; refactor around them as you need.
check: go build ./... && go test -count=1 -run '^TestIntegration$/^branch$/^sort_local_branches_in_stack_order$' ./pkg/integration/clients/ && go test -count=1 -run '^TestIntegration$/^branch$/^sort_remote_branches_in_stack_order$' ./pkg/integration/clients/
